label: Holdings Card
title: Holdings Card
summary: Use a Holdings Card for one loan offer or holding: its headline amount, its key terms, and a radio to choose it from a list.

configuration.title: Trailing, footer, and colours
configuration.description: The top right shows a Radio by default, for choosing this offer. badgeLabel swaps it for a status Badge, green by default; AppearanceSystem warning makes it orange. trailing swaps in your own component, and radio false leaves the top right empty. footer adds a divider, footerItems as labelled links, and a small Apply button that is always blue. children replaces the terms with your own content. AppearanceBrand colours the panel: Primary (pale gold) by default, Secondary (lilac), Neutral (white, as in Figma), or Tertiary (light grey).

states.title: Selected comes from your screen
states.description: The whole card is one button. When it’s pressed, your onPress sets selected, and the Radio fills; the card doesn’t select itself. disabled greys the Radio and stops presses. A card without onPress is disabled too, and then its footer links and button don’t respond to clicks either. While pressed, the card fades a little.

sizing.title: Give it a width
sizing.description: The card has no width of its own: it fills a host that stretches it, and shrinks to its content anywhere else. Set it with style, as Figma does at 328 px. The terms share the width in three equal columns, and the height follows the content: 20 px of padding at the top and bottom, 16 px at the sides, and 10 px between the parts. Each extra row of terms adds about 47 px.

content.title: Say what the number is
content.description: Make heroLabel say what the amount is, such as Loan amount up to, and give heroValue already formatted, with its ₹. Keep term labels to a word or two and put the unit in the value: 36 months, 12% p.a. Name footer links for the next step, and keep the action to one word, such as Apply. headerImage is made for a wide logo: a square mark sits centred in its 100 × 24 box. Holdings work the same way: the current value as the hero, with quantity and returns as terms.

sources.title: Use the public Holdings Card contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (19 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Holdings Card exposes children, footer, radio, and trailing; it is a white card (AppearanceBrand Neutral) with a dark badge and a gold Apply button. In the package, the default card is pale gold, the badge green, the footer links black, and the Apply button is always blue, whatever AppearanceBrand you set. The card has no width of its own, a card without onPress is disabled along with its footer, and it is about 7 px taller than Figma’s because its text lines are taller. A long badge is cut off by the card’s edge, and a two-word action wraps in the 80 px button. The published Storybook is older than the installed package and still shows the older generated page; its With image story can’t load its logo (all reported).
